'''Robert Rosebrugh''' is a Canadian [[Category theory|category theorist]] and [[Database theory|database theorist]]. He earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in mathematics in 1977 at [[Dalhousie University]] under the supervision of Robert Paré. He is a professor emeritus at [[Mount Allison University]].  He is a founding editor of the journal Theory and Applications of Categories and served as the managing editor from its founding in 1995 until 2020.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Gran |first=Marino |last2=Johnson |first2=Michael |last3=Tholen |first3=Walter |last4=Wood |first4=R. J. |date=2021-03-01 |title=In appreciation of Bob Rosebrugh |url=http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/volumes/36/fwd/36-fwd.pdf |journal=Theory and Applications of Categories |volume=36 |pages=1–8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosebrugh |first=Bob |date=6 Jan 1995 |title=Electronic Journal on Category Theory |url=https://mta.ca/~cat-dist/catlist/1999/elec-journal}}</ref>

Prior to the journal, in 1990 Rosebrugh created Categories, an internet [[Bulletin board system|bulletin board]] for category theory.<ref name=":0" /> In 2003, along with [[William Lawvere]], Rosebrugh published a book using [[Categorical Algebra|categorical algebra]] as a [[Foundations of mathematics|foundation]] and described the [[category of sets]] for a [[structural set theory]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Sets for mathematics |date=2003 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-01060-3 |editor-last=Lawvere |editor-first=Francis W. |location=Cambridge, UK New York |editor-last2=Rosebrugh |editor-first2=Robert}}</ref> Rosebrugh connected two theoretical approaches to database [[View (SQL)|view]] updates to lenses, a type of object studied in category theory, in a 2010 paper.<ref>{{Citation |last=Michael Johnson |title=Algebras and Update Strategies |url=https://lib.jucs.org/article/29630/ |access-date=2025-10-18 |publisher=Verlag der Technischen Universität Graz |doi=10.3217/JUCS-016-05-0729 |last2=Richard Wood |last3=Robert Rosebrugh}}</ref>

The journal Theory and Applications of Categories had a [[festschrift]] in his honor in 2021<ref name=":0" />
